subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Acme)

Thanks again for taking the time today, John — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum heading into the bake-off: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency at peak for your support search pipeline (95th pct spikes causing SLA misses)
- Secondary: high per-request cost for embeddings + need to unify models across internal and partner workflows
- Goal: replace the current multi-vendor stack with a single inference layer that meets 99th pct latency SLOs at 50k qps and reduces per-embedding cost by ~30%

Where Redwood stood in the meeting (high level)
- Strengths called out: predictable dedicated capacity, prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost, and clear quantization profiles for the embedding workload
- Open concerns you flagged: 1) baseline latency at 99th across live traffic, 2) integration effort for routing policies, 3) procurement/contract timeline

Competitive context (based on your notes)
- Current vendors you're validating: OmniAnalytics (existing vendor), Vertigo Models (open LLM partner), Redwood (us)
- Decision criteria you emphasized: latency at scale, consistency (SLA), integration effort (routing + retries), and TCO over 12 months

Proposed next steps
1) Share a short competitive matrix and the recording from today's demo — attached. (See competitive_matrix.xlsx)
2) Run a focused POC: 2-week bake-off where we replay a representative traffic sample (you provide) and we run Redwood Dedicated vs OmniAnalytics with identical model configs. Success criteria: 99th pct latency < 250ms, <30% uplift in cost vs baseline.
3) Tech check: Rafael will own a 30-min integration call to review routing and KV caching options next week.
4) Procurement: If POC metrics look good, we can fast-track SOW + pricing for a 6-month pilot. Vivek will support any SLA exceptions.

Open questions for you
- Can you share a 24–72h traffic dump (anonymized) or a smaller representative sample for the POC?
- Any hard constraints on data residency for this trial?
- Who from procurement should we include on the SOW conversations?

Attachments: competitive_matrix.xlsx, redwood-demo-recording.mp4, scope_of_work-draft.docx

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Rafael's tech check and a proposed POC timeline once I hear on the traffic sample.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

--

(Onward: quoted notes from today's call)
John: "We need something that won't introduce more variability — performance consistency is the tie-breaker for us."

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Acme)

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Traffic sample: I can get a 48-hour anonymized sample to you by end of day Monday. Will strip PII and any customer IDs.
2) Data residency: For the POC we can host in us-west only; production may require multi-region but not necessary for this test.
3) Procurement: Please loop in procurement@acme.com — they already handle proofs of concept agreements. For larger pilots we'll need a standard SOW + our legal review.

Open question: Do you have an existing test harness for replaying requests (headers + payloads) or do we need to build one? Also — curious about whether Redwood will instrument request-level tracing so we can correlate spikes to specific request shapes.

Happy to move Rafael's tech check to Tuesday morning PST. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

John
John Lee
Head of Search Engineering, Acme Corp
john.lee@acme.com

John — great, thanks for the quick replies and for confirming residency for the POC. A few answers and clarifications: 

- Traffic replay: We have an internal lightweight replay harness we can share — it accepts anonymized logs and can run at a configurable concurrency. Rafael will send the instructions plus a small Docker image. That should let us run both Redwood and OmniAnalytics against the same sample with minimal engineering.
- Tracing & correlation: Yes — we can turn on request-level tracing during the POC and provide a per-request CSV with timing breakdowns (ingest, KV lookup, model latency). We'll also provide 95/99/99.9 pct buckets by route.
- Timeline: Proposed POC window: Mar 1–14 (14 days). Rafael to lead the tech check on Tue 2/23 at 10:00 AM PST.
- Success criteria (clarified): 99th pct latency < 250ms for the support-search route under realistic concurrency; embedding cost delta target: <= +10% vs baseline (we think we can do -30% but will validate).

Next actions from Redwood
- Rafael: send replay harness and runbook + schedule tech check (assigned)
- Neha: I'll draft a concise SOW for a 6-week pilot that can be expanded to 6 months; will share initial draft by Wed 2/24
- Me: Send competitive matrix and demo recording (attached)

John — if that timeline works I'll put the invites on the calendar and Rafael will share the runbook.

Best,
Marissa

--

Key asks for the bake-off (internal)
- Rafael: Prepare the Docker replay image + a short checklist (what we need from Acme: sample format, anonymization notes, target concurrency)
- Neha: Draft SOW/estimated pricing for a 6-week POC and optional 6-month pilot (include our standard SLA and what upgrades would look like)
- Vivek: Stand by for procurement questions — Acme will loop procurement@acme.com; we may need a quick credit/exception review to meet their timeline.

Also please review the competitive matrix and call out any glaring gaps. We should be prepared with a short list of follow-up tests (KV cache enabled vs disabled, quantized model vs float baseline, and a cold-start stress test).

Thanks — Marissa
